system_prompt: You are assisting with a factual question about Thai law. State which provision applies and what it requires. Answer in English.
prompt: In June 2024, what wording did Section 1567(2) of the Thai Civil and Commercial Code, as then in force, use to define the limits of punishing a child? Quote the wording.
raw_response:
**Applicable provision:** Section 1567(2) of the Civil and Commercial Code of Thailand (ประมวลกฎหมายแพ่งและพาณิชย์ มาตรา ๑๕๖๗ (๒)), which enumerated the rights of a person exercising parental power (ผู้ใช้อำนาจปกครอง) over a minor child.

**Wording in force as of June 2024 (before the later 2024 amendment that removed this clause):**

Thai text:
> "(๒) ทำโทษบุตรตามสมควรเพื่อว่ากล่าวสั่งสอน"

Official English rendering:
> "(2) to punish the child in a reasonable manner for disciplinary purposes."

**What it required/limited:** This provision granted a parent (or person exercising parental power) the right to punish (ทำโทษ) the child, but only "ตามสมควร" — i.e., in a manner that was "reasonable" or "appropriate" — and only "เพื่อว่ากล่าวสั่งสอน," meaning for the purpose of admonishing or instructing/disciplining the child. Thus the punishment had to be proportionate and educational/corrective in nature, not punishment inflicted arbitrarily, excessively, or for purposes unrelated to the child's upbringing. This was the statutory basis, prior to the later legislative reform, permitting parents a limited right of corporal or other reasonable punishment for disciplinary ends.
